To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electronic structure of iron based superconducting materials is strongly influenced by the antiferromagnetic (AFM) correlations and their suppression by doping.

the electronic spectrum and FS of iron-pnictides (chalcogenides) close to the Fermion level can be described by the simplified analytic model, and that the evolution of FS and pseudogap formation in these compounds can be explained in the frame of this model.

the electronic structure of iron-pnictides and iron-chalcogenides is strongly influenced by the antiferromagnetic fluctuations and that these effects are more important in the electron doped compounds than in the hole doped ones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
electronic structure of iron based superconducting compounds, and the influence of magnetic scattering on the electronic spectrum and possible FS reconstruction.
the electronic structure and its relation to superconductivity in the iron-based superconductors, which are the most recent high-temperature superconductor family.
the study of electronic structure and possible pseudopgap behavior in iron based high-temperature supercondutors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no indications of a pseudogap in iron based superconductor, and the only possible pseudogap is connected with the short-range AFM order.
, in general, there are no strong arguments against a possible existence of pseudogap in the iron-pnictogen superconductors, but the situation is still far from clear.
the electronic structure of the Fe-pnictogen/chalcogen compounds is very rich and interesting, and that the ARPES measurements are a very important tool for its understanding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pseudogap is not the intrinsic property of the parent compound, but rather the effect of AFM fluctuations.
the AFM scattering in iron-pnictogen superconductors is very similar to that in cuprates, but the FS topology is different.
the pseudogap behavior can be naturally explained by the AFM fluctuations, without any additional assumptions about the electronic spectrum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electronic properties of iron-based superconductors in the region of AFM fluctuations and short-range order are similar to the cuprate case and can be described in the same way.

the electronic structure of the iron-based superconductors, including the possible pseudogap, can be qualitatively understood in the framework of the simple model, without any adjustable parameters, and that the main effect of doping is the modification of the Fermi surfaces, which are strongly affected by the AFM scattering.
AFM fluctuations are important and may lead to the pseudogap behavior, but they are not the only reason for the pseudogap.
